react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected system. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top hit with FDR = 5.56 × 10⁻¹⁸ and fold-enrichment = 778, capturing seven of the ten input metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms the same pathway as its sole genome-wide significant hit (p = 1.59 × 10⁻⁸) with six metabolites overlapping. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis returns MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism as the top-ranked pathway (p = 0.00126) with 17 of 18 pathway members matched, confirming robust empirical-compound network coverage. The serotonin/melatonin biosynthesis branch (REACT:R-HSA-209931) is separately enriched (FDR = 3.38 × 10⁻⁸) within the broader tryptophan umbrella, and the kynurenine-to-NAD⁺ branch is captured by WP:WP4210 (FDR = 1.46 × 10⁻¹⁰) and WP:WP3645 (FDR = 3.78 × 10⁻⁸). L-Tryptophan is the canonical upstream substrate for all three branches. The driver signal compounds are serotonin (KEGG:C00780), melatonin (KEGG:C01598), 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (KEGG:C00632), quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722), and tryptamine (KEGG:C00398), all of which are documented intermediates in the serotonin/melatonin pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931) and the kynurenine branch (WP:WP5044). Indoleacetaldehyde (KEGG:C00637) appears in the serotonin/melatonin branch hit list. L-Valine (KEGG:C00183) and 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (KEGG:C03912) contribute to a secondary proline/valine metabolism signal (MUMM:arginine_and_proline_metabolism, p = 0.026) and are likely unrelated upstream metabolites, not driver tryptophan intermediates. The biological story is a coordinated perturbation of tryptophan catabolism affecting both the neuroactive biogenic-amine branch (serotonin-melatonin) and the immunomodulatory kynurenine branch leading to NAD⁺ biosynthesis, consistent with a systemic inflammatory or tryptophan-challenge experimental condition.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant affected system. RaMP multi-DB ORA identifies KEGG:map00380 (Tryptophan metabolism) as the top hit with FDR = 5.56 × 10⁻¹⁸, capturing seven of the ten input metabolites (L-tryptophan, melatonin, quinolinic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, serotonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, and tryptamine). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00380 as its sole genome-wide significant hit (p = 1.59 × 10⁻⁸, six overlapping metabolites: L-tryptophan, melatonin, serotonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers Tryptophan metabolism as its top pathway (p = 0.00202, 17 of 18 matched compounds). Cross-paradigm consensus on L-tryptophan (KEGG:C00078), serotonin (KEGG:C00780), and melatonin (KEGG:C01598) as signal compounds is confirmed across all three tools. Secondary enrichment for valine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00290, p = 0.0444) reflects L-valine (KEGG:C00183) as a single-hit pathway. A secondary cross-tool consensus on Arginine and Proline Metabolism (MUMM:arginine_and_proline_metabolism, p = 0.030) captures 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid (KEGG:C03912) and pyrroline hydroxycarboxylic acid (KEGG:C04281). The tryptophan metabolic network is further supported by the IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR = 1.36 × 10⁻⁸) and by the Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis module (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR = 3.38 × 10⁻⁸), which captures L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin. Tryptophan catabolism leading to NAD+ production (WP:WP4210, FDR = 1.46 × 10⁻¹⁰) captures L-tryptophan, quinolinic acid, serotonin, and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, placing the kynurenine-branch metabolites in the same pathway context as the neuroactive intermediates.
